data.name: Mahesh
data.gender_notes: Mahesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Mahesh is a name derived from the Sanskrit language, representing the Hindu god Shiva, the Supreme Lord and the ruler of the universe. He is also known as the Lord of the Mountains. The name Mahesh carries the meaning “Lord of the Mountains” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mahesh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mountains and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Mahesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Mountains.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mahesh total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mahesh is deeply rooted in the Hindu culture, carrying with it the powerful symbolism of the revered deity, Lord Shiva. He is regarded as the "God of Gods," and is worshiped across India and Nepal. The name evokes a sense of strength, resilience, and protection, reflecting the legendary tales and mythological significance of Lord Shiva in Hindu mythology and philosophy.
data.spiritual_significance: Mahesh is a name filled with spiritual potency and deep meaning. It represents the divine, omnipresent energy and consciousness that underlies the universe. In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is considered as the embodiment of this cosmic consciousness and supreme power, absorbing and transforming all that exists. The name Mahesh is a reminder that everything in the universe, including ourselves, is an expression of the divine consciousness. Hence, the name Mahesh asserts a profound spiritual connection and a call to remember and honor the divine within ourselves and the world around us.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mahesh symbolizes the destructive and transformative aspect of Shiva, the God of Gods in Hinduism. His name signifies the power to annihilate and recreate the universe, embodying the cyclical nature of existence.

vedic_reference.note: One of the many names for Lord Shiva, the god of destruction and creation.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mahabharata, Anusasana Parva, Section 92 The name Mahesh carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mahesh is mentioned as one of the names of Rudra, a form of Shiva. In this text, it is stated that Mahesh is the lord of the universe, the supporter of all, and the giver of boons.
